newsitem.title: DUBAI: British Bank of Middle East lifts attributable profit.
newsitem.headline: British Bank of Middle East lifts attributable profit.

text.p: The British Bank of the Middle East (BritishBank) said on Monday it lifted attributable profit to 62 million pounds in 1996 from 58 million in 1995.
BritishBank is a subsidiary of HSBC Holdings, which earlier on Monday announced a 23 percent rise in pre-tax profits to 4.52 billion pounds in 1996.

"The British Bank of the Middle East recorded a satisfactory performance in 1996, mainly due to an increase in net interest income and higher net fees and commissions earned on our trade finance related activities, and from card products," said deputy chairman Aman Mehta in a statement.
Net interest income rose 16 percent, mainly because of a 49 percent increase in customer advances. Operating profit before provisions was up 14 percent at 95 million pounds.
Pre-tax profit was up nine percent at 84 million pounds.
The bank said its UAE car finance subsidiary Middle East Finance Co showed substantial profit growth, with a net profit of 2.5 million pounds from 1995's 1.7 million pounds.
BritishBank has operations in Jordan, Lebanon, Bahrain, Qatar, Oman and the United Arab Emirates. It also operates in the Bahamas, India, Switzerland and the United Kingdom.
During the year a branch was opened in Baku, Azerbaijan.
The bank said it had been granted a licence to open a branch in Ramallah in the West Bank.
